issues.legal_issue: Deadly force is justified in private defence of the body when an assault creates a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt and the force used does not exceed what is necessary for defence.
material_facts: A large group went to remove a bund by force despite knowing that those guarding it would resist and that one of them had a gun.
The group attacked the defenders, severely beating older members and causing numerous injuries, including injuries to vital parts of the body.
The gun was used against the attacking group when the person using it apprehended grave danger to the lives of the defenders and to himself.
The occupiers had time to seek relief from public authorities or the pending civil court, but instead went to remove the bund by force.
The court found that the person who used the gun did not exceed the right of private defence.
issues.conclusion: The use of the gun was justified in the exercise of the right of private defence, and the accused were entitled to acquittal.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 96 and 97 of the Indian Penal Code, acts done in private defence are not offences and a person may defend their own body or another person's body against offences affecting the human body. Subject to the restrictions in section 99, section 100 permits causing death where an assault reasonably creates an apprehension that death or grievous hurt will otherwise result; section 99 limits the right where there is time to seek public protection and prohibits inflicting more harm than necessary. The right is preventive, not punitive, and must be applied practically; the judgment refers to Munshi Ram v. Delhi Administration and Kishna v. State of Rajasthan in describing its social purpose.

rule.if: criminal_case_for_causing_death_or_injury and opposing_group_uses_force and assault_creates_reasonable_fear_of_death_or_grievous_hurt and force_used_is_not_excessive

predicates.criminal_case_for_causing_death_or_injur: The accused is prosecuted for causing another person's death or injury.
predicates.opposing_group_uses_force: The opposing group uses force against the accused or people the accused is defending.
predicates.assault_creates_reasonable_fear_of_death: The assault is of a kind that reasonably causes the accused to fear death or grievous hurt to themselves or another person.
predicates.force_used_is_not_excessive: The accused uses no more force than is reasonably required for defence.

issues.definition: When a person prosecuted for causing death or injury faces a forceful assault that reasonably threatens death or grievous hurt, their force is justified if it is not excessive.

issues.legal_issue: A court may give an accused the benefit of private defence when the evidence establishes it even if the accused did not raise that plea and instead relied on an inconsistent defence.
material_facts: The accused who used the gun denied being present and relied on an alibi.
The evidence and other relevant material nevertheless established the circumstances in which he used the gun and supported private defence.
The High Court rejected private defence in part because the accused had not pleaded it.
issues.conclusion: The accused's alibi did not prevent the court from applying private defence on the evidence, and the court was required to consider that evidence rather than reject the defence for want of a plea.
issues.legal_principle: A court should not ignore evidence establishing private defence merely because an accused raised a different defence, such as alibi. The law of private defence is to be administered practically and with reasonable liberality to give effect to its preventive purpose; technical rules of civil pleadings and estoppel do not bar its application. The judgment discusses sections 96 to 106 of the Indian Penal Code and refers to Munshi Ram v. Delhi Administration and Kishna v. State of Rajasthan for the underlying social purpose of the right.

predicates.criminal_case_for_causing_death_or_injur: The accused is prosecuted for causing another person's death or injury.
predicates.evidence_establishes_private_defence: The evidence and relevant material establish circumstances supporting the accused's exercise of private defence.
predicates.accused_raises_inconsistent_defence: The accused relies on a defence, such as alibi, that differs from private defence.

issues.definition: In a prosecution for causing death or injury, a court may apply private defence where the evidence establishes it, even if the accused relied on a different defence.
